newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAEL'S INTERNAL DEBT UP 2.3 PERCENT IN 1ST HALF.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL'S INTERNAL DEBT UP 2.3 PERCENT IN 1ST HALF.

text.p: The Israeli government's internal debt rose by a real 2.3 percent in the first half of 1997 to 263 billion shekels, the central bank said on Wednesday.
In the last decade the internal debt rose at a real rate of 23 percent.
It said government bonds in public hands had fallen from 54 percent of public financial assets in 1990 to 39 percent in mid-1997, mainly because of overseas government fundraising.

The central bank said non-traded government debt as a percentage of internal debt had fallen in recent years in line with monetary policy to increase debt tradeability but said that about half of Israel's internal debt was still non-tradeable.
